name: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Ltd
title: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Ltd - 544658 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Industry equity AUM fell 0.4% QoQ while ICICI Pru AMC equity AUM grew 2% QoQ to INR6.2tn, with Q4 PAT down 16.8% QoQ on mark-to-market losses and ESOP timing; no supply-side levers apply to an AMC.

summary.headline: ICICI Pru AMC Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 19.5% YoY to INR15.17bn, while PAT fell 16.8% QoQ to INR7.63bn on negative other income.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue reached INR15.17bn (up 19.5% YoY, 0.2% QoQ), with operating PBT of INR11.28bn (up 30.2% YoY). PAT of INR7.63bn was up 10.4% YoY but down 16.8% QoQ, driven mainly by a INR0.89bn negative other income from mark-to-market losses. Management said the company held its equity AUM share at 14.2% while industry equity AUM fell 0.4% QoQ. Management flagged the ICICI Ventures AIF transfer effective 1 April 2026 and a 3-4 bps gross TER impact from the 1 April regulatory change.

financial_highlights.value: INR12.4 per share, subject to shareholder approval

segments.name: Mutual fund (total)
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM INR11.05trn, up 2.6% QoQ and 25.6% YoY; market share 13.5%, #2 AMC. FY26 margins: equity 67 bps, debt 32 bps, liquid 12 bps, passive 10 bps, arbitrage 30 bps.

segments.name: Equity and equity-oriented
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM INR6.2trn, up 2% QoQ and 27.2% YoY; market share 14.2%, largest. Industry equity AUM declined 0.4% QoQ.

segments.name: Equity hybrid
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM INR2.18trn, up 4.5% QoQ and 31.8% YoY; market share 26.7%, largest.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM INR1.99trn, down 2.7% QoQ and up 15.6% YoY, in line with industry.

segments.name: Passive
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM INR1.84trn, up 10% QoQ and 48.3% YoY.

segments.name: Active schemes
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM INR9.21trn, 13.7% market share, up 1.3% QoQ and 21.9% YoY.

segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM INR729.95bn. PMS INR268.27bn (down 1.7% QoQ, up 26.7% YoY); AIF INR170.33bn (up 7.1% QoQ, 47.3% YoY). FY26 gross yield 2.0%, net yield 0.98%.

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: FY26 yield on assets under advisory 0.33%. Revenue share 1.77% of Q4 net revenue.

guidance_outlook: Regulatory TER change effective 1 April 2026: gross impact of 3-4 bps before payouts; mitigation steps underway, crystallised impact to be shared in about two months.
ESOP/ESU grant: total non-cash cost INR1.2-1.3bn amortised over vesting; P&L debit of INR640-680m in FY27, INR360-400m in FY28, INR180-220m in FY29.

ICICI Ventures AIF investment management transferred; company manages these AIFs from 1 April 2026 with fee-paying committed funds of INR46.28bn across PE, early-stage PE and affordable real estate strategies.
Management gave no explicit FY27 opex guidance, saying growth would be on a normalised basis.
One or two NFOs expected next month (May), subject to regulator approval, from a pipeline of four to five ideas across SIF and MF.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation disclosures in the call; the transcript contains no capacity or utilisation figures.

Capital deployment: the company's own investment book is largely seed money to be deployed; the balance is held for opportunistic deployment with no specific allocation by asset class (per Q&A on investment book).

ESOP/ESU non-cash cost of INR1.2-1.3bn (Black-Scholes, approved by NRC) to be amortised over the three-year vesting period; P&L debit of INR640-680m in FY27, INR360-400m in FY28 and INR180-220m in FY29.
Launch pipeline: four to five ideas under regulatory review across SIF and MF; one or two NFOs possible in May 2026 subject to regulator approval.

Expansion footprint: GIFT City retail FME branch presence with the first IFSC offering (Cat 3 AIF, ICICI Prudential Smart Navigator Fund, launched February 2026); DIFC office in Dubai established with a dedicated team.
demand_pricing: Industry Q4 FY26 quarterly average AUM INR81.62trn, up 21.1% YoY and 0.7% QoQ; equity AUM INR43.80trn, down 0.4% QoQ; Nifty 50 fell 14.5% in the quarter to 22,331.
Industry equity net inflows INR1.24trn in Q4, up QoQ despite falling markets; March 2026 industry SIP contribution INR32,087 crore vs INR31,002 crore in December 2025.
Company systematic transactions (SIP and STP) INR51.04bn in March 2026, up 1.3% QoQ and 30.6% YoY.
Equity distribution mix: direct 28.9%, MFDs 36.7%, ICICI Bank 7.9%, other banks 11%, national distributors 15.5%. Net flow market share in equity exceeds AUM market share.
Management said yields on new AIF/PE business are in line with industry, with no specific figure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sequential revenue and profit decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the QoQ profit decline mainly to negative other income from mark-to-market; core revenue was broadly flat with a small increase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net AIF/PMS yield rise to 0.98% from 0.91%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects product mix, with occasional benefits such as exit charges also contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the blended MF yield fall about 1.4 bps QoQ (47.5 to 46.1)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it was driven by a higher ETF mix in the quarterly average AUM; MF operating yield was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost decline sequential run-rate and what is the ESOP impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a component of compensation was replaced by ESOP/ESU, with no P&L debit in Q4; ESOP costs will be debited from FY27 per the schedule given. Run-rate ex-ESOP is the base, with normal increments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ICICI Ventures AUM and consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee-paying committed funds of INR46.28bn move to the company from 1 April 2026; consideration paid was described as not material.

qa_highlights.question: What is the iSIF investor profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said iSIF customers are largely fresh, with no migration from PMS, given the INR10 lakh iSIF ticket versus about INR50 lakh PMS entry.

qa_highlights.question: Is there market share loss in SIPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the SIP flow trend is structurally positive quarter-on-quarter and that March was better, without addressing share loss directly.

risks_watch: Equity industry AUM and flows are sensitive to market drawdowns and geopolitical uncertainty; management said April trends were similar to March but it is too early to call.
Regulatory TER change from 1 April 2026 (3-4 bps gross impact) and the outcome of the mitigation plan due in about two months.
Mark-to-market volatility on the treasury and investment book keeps other income under pressure.
Rising ESOP costs (INR640-680m in FY27) will weigh on reported employee expense.
Management declined to give FY27 opex guidance, so cost trajectory is unclear.
Alternates yield (PMS 2.0% gross, 0.98% net) and the integration of ICICI Ventures AIFs need to be tracked.
SIP stoppages and ticket-size trends in the industry data.
summary.management_tone: Confident on market share and structural SIP flows, but cautious and noncommittal on near-term flows and April trends. Management gave few forward numbers, deferring the TER impact and opex growth until later updates.
key_quotes: So people understand that this mutual fund is a long -term instrument. In equity, you make money over the long term.
We have to bother about out of INR100 coming into the industry, what comes to us?
So we get a lot of flows on the multi-asset funds from a customer point of view.
There is no much difference that we see between March and April, right?

growth.why: No explicit FY27 revenue or opex guidance; growth framed on a normalised basis, with a 3-4 bps gross TER hit from 1 April and one or two NFOs possible in May from a pipeline of four to five ideas, so backing is vague and the outlook is flat.
